parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both services concern appointments, so they share a broad topic. They are not built the same way, though. SchedulingService works through persistence DAOs (PatientDao, AppointmentDao). It turns each row into a domain entity (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment), puts the rules in those entities (isMinor, treatsMinors, overlaps, cancel) and reports failures with SchedulingError. VisitNotesService injects PrismaService and calls prisma.visitNote.create/findMany itself. It skips any DAO. It declares its own VisitNote shape inside the service file instead of a domain entity. It never checks the appointment through the Appointment abstraction (it writes notes for any appointmentId) and it does not use the module's error type. That is a bypass of the module's own data-access and entity pattern. SchedulingService also has its own duplication: it builds an Appointment from a stored row with the same code in two places, in book() for the same-day list and in cancel(). That mapping should live in one place. The ID-generation scheme also differs between the two files: an `apt-${this.next++}` in-memory counter versus `${appointmentId}:${Date.now()}`. This review only covers abstraction consistency. Which layer may import which is checked by other tools.

violations.message: Skips the module's DAO and entity pattern: it injects PrismaService and calls prisma.visitNote.create/findMany directly, and declares its own VisitNote shape in the service instead of using a domain entity. SchedulingService uses PatientDao/AppointmentDao and entities from ../entities. It also writes notes without checking the appointment through the Appointment abstraction.

The row-to-Appointment mapping (`new Appointment(a.id, a.patientId, a.practitionerId, a.startsAt, a.minutes, a.status as AppointmentStatus)`) is written twice, in book() and in cancel(), instead of in one place.
